What is the exact requirement of INV-01?

Per INV-01: *(amended — D-027, D-028; PC-assignment resolved as a visible stage per D-036)* A JO's lifecycle stage is derived from its rows. A single-track, single-branch JO — the common case — has exactly one row and therefore exactly one stage, unchanged from original behavior: Submitted, **PC Assignment**, In Layout, Internal Review, Revision, External Review (flag, not a stage — see INV-04), Pending Release, In-House Printing, Sent to Purchasing, Closed, or Cancelled. Never zero, never more than one, for that row. **PC Assignment sits between Submitted and In Layout** — it's the real moment the PC picks an artist, with its own actor and timestamp, not a background write folded silently into Submitted (see LC-17). A JO with multiple branches and/or multiple tracks (digital + printed on the same branch) decomposes into one (branch, track) row per active track, and **each row carries its own independent stage** — one branch's digital track can sit in Sent to Purchasing while its printed track is still in Revision. **The JO itself has no independent stage** — it exposes only an aggregate summary derived from its rows (e.g. "2 of 4 rows done"), never a single stage value standing in for the whole JO.

What is the exact requirement of INV-02?

Per INV-02: CD sign-off happens **inside Internal Review** — Art Director review is optional per JO, Creative Director sign-off is always required, and CD can approve without AD ever having seen it. No JO reaches Internal Approved without a CD stamp. **Pending Release requires no further approval** — it is the Requestor's explicit go-signal plus print-route choice (in-house vs. Purchasing), not a second CD gate.

What is the exact requirement of INV-03?
Per INV-03: Closed JOs cannot be edited. The only way to change a Closed JO is Reopen (LC-10), which is itself a logged, reason-required action — not a silent edit.

What is the exact requirement of INV-04?
Per INV-04: External Review is a flag/attribute on a JO, never a lifecycle stage. Raising or clearing it never changes the JO's actual stage.

What is the exact requirement of INV-05?
Per INV-05: Every revision cycle increments the JO's revision count. The count never decreases (reopening for a new revision adds to the count, it doesn't reset it).

What is the exact requirement of INV-06?

Per INV-06: A JO always belongs to exactly one Requestor. It has exactly one Primary Artist by default, once claimed. **Amended (D-013, resolved)**: individual placements within a JO may be overridden to a named artist other than the Primary Artist — this is a placement-level exception, not a repeal of the rule. A JO without any placement-level overrides still has exactly one accountable artist, full stop. **Assign/reassign authority is PC-exclusive** — see INV-26 for the narrower set of roles that may also cancel or hold a JO without reassigning it.

What is the exact requirement of INV-07?

Per INV-07: *(reversed — Ed's review, July 29)* Comments **can be edited**, reversing the previous immutable-only rule. An edit is never silent: the comment carries a visible "edited" indicator that expands to show what changed, and editing fires a notification to everyone already on that thread — same fan-out as posting a new comment. What's preserved from the old rule: there's still no silent, untracked overwrite — the edit history itself is the permanent record, in place of "immutable, correction via new comment only."

What is the exact requirement of INV-08?
Per INV-08: Every Activity entry (comment, revision note, approval, reassignment) has an author and a timestamp. No anonymous or undated entries.

What is the exact requirement of INV-09?
Per INV-09: Every upload belongs to exactly one JO. No orphaned or shared attachments.

What is the exact requirement of INV-10?

Per INV-10: The Approval Sheet stamp, once applied, is permanent and binding — it is the record of who approved what, when, on which version. It cannot be un-stamped; a reversal happens through Reopen, not by erasing the stamp. **Extended (Ed's review, July 29):** the sign-off action itself can only be performed from inside the Approval Sheet page — the approver has to actually open and review it first. Any dashboard-level or list-level UI may display sign-off status, but must never expose the sign-off action directly, precisely so nobody can stamp a JO without opening it.

What is the exact requirement of INV-11?
Per INV-11: Every version-tagged entry (comment, revision) refers to a specific, immutable version number. Version numbers only increment, never get reused or renumbered.

What is the exact requirement of INV-12?
Per INV-12: The internal AD/CD review channel is never visible to PC or Requestor, regardless of role-switching or view. They see generic stage state only.

What is the exact requirement of INV-13?

Per INV-13: *(widened — Ed's review, July 29, "My JO Requests" / "All JO Requests")* There is one **Requestor-tier** of visibility — everything a Requestor can see about their own JO (fields, status, comments at that tier, revisions per INV-24) — and every Requestor now sees that same tier on **every** JO, not only ones they filed themselves. This is what "My JO Requests" vs. "All JO Requests" means at the data layer: same tier, different scope (mine vs. everyone's), so a Requestor can check for an existing/duplicate request before filing. **AD and CD get this Requestor-tier on every JO, plus their existing internal-review tier** (INV-12) — they don't lose anything, they gain the same baseline everyone else has. PC/Purchasing visibility is unaffected by this change (per existing role scope).

What is the exact requirement of INV-14?
Per INV-14: A Requestor scoped to a specific JO type (e.g. Aldrin→Board Up) cannot file outside that type through any path, including the "type a name not listed" custom fallback.

What is the exact requirement of INV-15?

Per INV-15: A flag (deadline-breach, workload-imbalance, revision soft-cap, dormancy) is always computed live from current state — never a stored value that can drift out of sync with the data that produced it.

What is the exact requirement of INV-16?
Per INV-16: Passive flags (deadline-breach) never escalate to push/urgent alerts on their own. Escalation, if it ever happens, is a deliberate design decision, not a default.

What is the exact requirement of INV-17?

Per INV-17: Every revision record captures its origin — which role raised it, and at what point in the lifecycle (during the original Internal Review loop, or as a post-approval revision raised by the Requestor or by Purchasing on a supplier's behalf). Origin is immutable once set, same principle as INV-07 governing comments.

What is the exact requirement of INV-18?

Per INV-18: A post-approval revision's return address is **derived from its origin, never manually chosen** by whoever completes the rework. AD/CD-raised revisions (never left the building) loop back to Internal Review per the existing rule. Requestor-raised revisions go straight to the artist — visible to PC/AD/CD as they happen — then back through Internal Review, then auto-return to Purchasing. **Corrected (Jul 28, Design system compliance session — was previously stated as "Purchasing-raised returns directly to Purchasing," which described the end but skipped how it gets there):** the full chain for a Purchasing-raised revision is **Purchasing → PC → Artist → Internal Review → Purchasing**. The destination hasn't changed — it still ends back at Purchasing, same as before. What was wrong is the *first* hop: Purchasing does not trigger the Artist directly. Purchasing notifies the PC, and the PC is the one who fires the trigger to the artist — same as any other assignment. This keeps assignment authority with the PC (INV-06/INV-26) even when the revision originates outside the creative team; Purchasing doesn't get a special bypass just because it's external. No UI may present the completing party with a choice of where to send it next; the destination is computed. This is the mechanism that prevents "approved but nobody forwarded it" from becoming a silent failure mode.

What is the exact requirement of INV-19?
Per INV-19: In-House Printing routes to the **Artist**, not Purchasing, as a go-ahead to print. AD, CD, and PC are notified of the routing choice for visibility but are not owners of the action.

What is the exact requirement of INV-20?

Per INV-20: An RS# (Requisition/Release Slip number) is optional, and applies only to externally-routed printable materials going through Purchasing to an outside vendor requiring mall/landlord sign-off. Free printing and Digital Placements never carry an RS# under any circumstance. For those two routes, the only gating condition is whether the Artist's final file link exists yet — presence of the link is what enables the send action, not any numbered field.

What is the exact requirement of INV-27?

Per INV-27: *(new — Jul 28, Design system compliance session)* **Purchasing is a parent stage, not a peer of "Printing."** Where a row's track requires Purchasing custody (i.e. it's going to an outside vendor per INV-20), the row enters **Purchasing**, and "Printing" is a **sub-status inside Purchasing** — sent to supplier — not a separate stage of its own. Purchasing marks the row **Done** once print comes back. This does not change INV-19's in-house exception: a row that doesn't need Purchasing custody at all skips this entire parent stage and routes straight back to the Artist. The branch point is "does this row need Purchasing custody" (yes → Purchasing, with Printing as its sub-state, → Done; no → straight back to Artist), not "who owns Printing."

What is the exact requirement of INV-29?

Per INV-29: A Placement is a **flat record** — description, W×H, unit, orientation, quantity, remarks, floor/location, phone#, landline# all sit on one record, no further nesting. **Corrects D-019's "Branch → Placement → Sizes"** — there is no separate Sizes sub-level; sizes are just fields on the Placement itself. The real hierarchy is **Mall/Place → Branch → Placement** — one mall can host multiple distinct branches (e.g. EO Store, Kids & Up-Supermarket, Active Eye-Supermarket, Kiosk, all at the same mall), each branch owns its own placement list. A Placement record and one item row on the JO filing form are **the same schema** — filing a JO item is creating (or reusing, via the Placement Bank) a Placement record, not a separate shape that needs mapping.

What is the exact requirement of INV-30?

Per INV-30: The 10 filing categories — Collaterals, Ecomm, Digital Placement, SGU, Store Opening, Board Up, Signage, POP, Voucher, Special Project — are the actual official JO-type list, **replacing** the older 6-type enumeration (Collaterals, Directional Signages, Voucher/POP, Digital Placements, Store Graphics Update/Store Opening, Board Up) wherever it appears in Spec v4 or elsewhere. These same 10 categories double as the secondary sort axis inside the Universal Placement Bank — primary sort is by branch, secondary sort within a branch is by category (some categories, especially Collaterals, contain many distinct placement types nested underneath).

What is the exact requirement of INV-23?

Per INV-23: *(corrected — Ed's review, July 29; supersedes the action-lock version. Scope clarified — Round 16)* The presence rule on Internal Review (D-021, AD-07/CD-06) is an **entry-lock**, not an action-lock. Whichever of AD/CD opens a **placement's** Approval Sheet first **locks the other out of entering that same placement at all** — not just out of approving. The second person cannot open that specific placement's sheet while the first is inside it. A visible "currently viewed by [name]" note is shown wherever the block happens, so the second person knows why and by whom. Lock releases when the first viewer navigates away or completes their action. **This corrects the previous version, which locked only the approve/return buttons while still allowing simultaneous viewing** — Ed's point: viewing alone isn't the conflict, since a JO's approval might genuinely belong to the other reviewer, not both; entry itself is what needs to be exclusive, not just the final click. **Scope (D-052, Round 16):** the lock is per-placement-instance, not per-JO. Given INV-33's partial-sheet model, AD and CD routinely work as parallel lanes clearing different placements on the same JO simultaneously — that's the intended throughput model, not a race condition. The lock only ever applies to two people trying to enter the *same* placement's sheet at the same moment.

What is the exact requirement of INV-24?

Per INV-24: A Requestor sees: revisions they raised themselves, revisions raised by Purchasing on their JO (per INV-18's routing, even though the revision itself passes through the PC), and the final released version. They do **not** see the internal AD/CD Internal Review back-and-forth (INV-12 still holds) or PC-internal reassignment chatter.

What is the exact requirement of INV-25?

Per INV-25: Reopen (LC-10) sends a Closed JO to the **PC**, who reassigns it — same artist or a new one, PC's call, same authority as any other assignment (INV-06). It does **not** go to Internal Review directly; the PC routes it from there per normal assignment. Both the **Requestor** and the **PC** may trigger a reopen; the reason-required logging rule (INV-03) applies regardless of who triggers it.

What is the exact requirement of INV-26?

Per INV-26: Assign and reassign authority is PC-exclusive (INV-06). **Cancel and hold are broader**: AD, CD, PC, and the Requestor may each cancel or place a JO on hold — none of these four needs to route the action through the PC first, unlike assignment.

What is the exact requirement of INV-21?

Per INV-21: Mall Admin Approval is a flag/attribute on a row (per INV-01's row model), never a lifecycle stage — same principle as INV-04 governing External Review. It is optional and Requestor-triggered: raised only when that specific row needs mall/landlord sign-off before release, sitting after Internal Review and before the print/release branch. Raising or clearing it never changes the row's actual stage.

What is the exact requirement of INV-22?

Per INV-22: A JO's deadline is JO-level by default (+3 days per LC-01), and may be overridden at the branch level, and further overridden at the track level within that branch. The most specific override in the cascade governs; where no override exists at a level, it falls through to the next level up. This mirrors INV-06's placement-level artist override — a targeted exception, not a repeal of the JO-level default.
You are the EO Creative Ops Compliance Engine. You provide verbatim rules from EO_System_Invariants_v8.md.
What is the exact requirement of INV-28?

Per INV-28: *(new — Jul 28, Design system compliance session)* **The full sequence after Internal Review approval, spelled out** — INV-21 states Mall Admin Approval is an optional flag; this invariant fixes what happens around it, which was previously undocumented: 1. Internal Review clears. 2. **If raised**, Mall Admin Approval must clear before the row proceeds (INV-21). If not raised, skip straight to step 3. 3. Requestor nudges the Artist for the final file — **skipped if the Artist already provided the final link** (e.g. it was already a WeTransfer/Drive link attached earlier). 4. The row's media type determines what happens next, independently per row (this is why combo JOs close their tracks asynchronously — see INV-01): - **Digital track**: Requestor sends the final link directly to whoever needs it. Row marks Done. Purchasing is never involved. - **Printed track**: Requestor sends the final link, plus an RS# if the print vendor requires one (INV-20), to **Purchasing**. The row then follows INV-27 — Purchasing custody, Printing as sub-status, Purchasing marks Done. A JO with both a digital and a printed row is not "released" as one action — each row's release is independent, exactly like their lifecycle stages are independent.

What is the exact requirement of INV-31?

Per INV-31: The for-approval proxy upload for a placement is checked for proportion against that JO row's own declared W×H — not against a separate Material/Placement library lookup. The check is aspect ratio within a ~2–3% tolerance band (absorbs normal export rounding); an orientation mismatch (landscape vs. portrait) is a hard flag regardless of tolerance. **This is never a submission block.** Out-of-tolerance shows a visible mismatch badge/stamp adjacent to the artwork — it never covers or obscures the design itself — plus an explicit "Upload as-is" override the Artist must click to proceed, with an optional free-text reason field. Every override is logged: who, which placement, timestamp, and the reason if one was given.

What is the exact requirement of INV-32?

Per INV-32: The for-approval proxy (small JPG/PNG/MP4/PDF) and the final deliverable (TIFF, hi-res MP4, or PDF) are never the same artifact. The proxy exists only to be checked and approved; it is never the file that gets delivered. The final deliverable continues to be gated by the existing link-presence rule (INV-20) — nothing about the proxy changes when a link becomes actionable.

What is the exact requirement of INV-33?

Per INV-33: An approval sheet is **not fixed to a JO's full placement set** — it is whatever subset of placements the Artist submits together, from one up to all of them. Each sheet, once approved, **releases immediately and independently**: its placements reflect as approved on the JO and release to the Requestor without waiting on any placement not yet in review. Purchasing's visibility and sheet access (INV-27, D-048) open on this same per-sheet basis — Purchasing may hold a partial placement set from one JO while the rest are still clearing review, and any partial view shown to Purchasing must indicate the count of placements still pending so it is never mistaken for the full order. Once **every** placement on the JO has cleared — across however many sheets it took — the system auto-compiles a final combined sheet covering all of them; this is generated, not manually reassembled. The final sheet stamps each placement with whichever approver actually cleared it — AD or CD, independently per placement — since INV-23's per-placement entry-lock means both can be clearing different placements on the same JO in parallel. Mixed AD/CD attribution across one compiled sheet is expected, not an error state.

What is the exact requirement of INV-34?

Per INV-34: A placement-level revision (as distinct from a full JO reopen, which stays governed by INV-25) routes according to the JO's current state, not according to who raised it: - **JO still open/ongoing** → routes directly to whoever already owns the placement (the Artist), with the PC notified for visibility, not as a blocking step. This applies whether the Requestor flagged the placement or the Artist self-raised the revision; a self-raised revision on an ongoing JO goes straight to Internal Review, skipping the PC and Requestor entirely. - **JO fully closed** → routes to the PC first, who reassigns — same pattern as INV-25. If the placement being revised was already approved and released to the Requestor, the Requestor is notified, and the PC is notified as well (symmetric with the Requestor-flagged case, even where the PC has no reassignment action available).

What is the exact requirement of INV-35?

Per INV-35: A JO's Requestor-facing status must always be shown as a per-placement breakdown (e.g. "7 approved · 2 in revision · 1 pending"), each entry drillable to that placement's actual stage. The JO's single top-level status label may only read "Closed" once every placement has cleared; at any other point, the breakdown is shown, never a single aggregate word standing in for a JO that is only partially resolved.
You are the EO Creative Ops Compliance Engine. You provide verbatim rules from EO_System_Invariants_v8.md.
What is the exact requirement of INV-36?

Per INV-36: Remarks belong to the placement/item, never to the JO as a whole. A JO form has no global remarks field. Every item row (Collaterals, Signages, SGU) carries its own remarks input; single-spec types (Voucher, Digital Placements, Board Up) each carry exactly one remarks field tied to that one entry. This exists because a single multi-branch JO can carry unrelated item types simultaneously (a banner at one branch, a voucher at another) — a shared remarks box has no way to express that a die-cut-bleed note belongs to the banner and a promo-period note belongs to the voucher.
You are the EO Creative Ops Compliance Engine. You provide verbatim rules from EO_System_Invariants_v8.md.
What is the exact requirement of INV-37?

Per INV-37: *(new — Round 19, formalized from a Round 18 build note that hadn't yet been given a number)* Once a JO's placements enter PC Assignment, the submitted data becomes immutable. There is no raw-edit path past this point for any role, including the Requestor. All subsequent changes happen exclusively through the tracked revision workflows already defined — INV-34's placement-level revision paths, or INV-25's reopen for a fully closed JO. This is why revisions carry a note, an initiator, and a routing rule instead of just silently overwriting a field: the record of *what changed and who changed it* matters as much as the change itself. ---
